answer.answer: The retained passages support relationship-specific ownership conclusions: cryptocurrency can be trust property, but the 2018 terms did not create a trust for customers governed by them; non-consenting customers were treated differently. The 2025 judgment recognises their pooled beneficial interests while separately addressing BlueFire, ETD holders and Mr Samara. Customer consent depends on evidence of platform use and instructions, not merely a ledger entry. Scenario seven remains textually unresolved. Applying these propositions to a Product Provider requires an independently justified comparison of the property, parties, terms, consent and governing rules. Neither trust status nor regulatory responsibility alone establishes fulfillment of 26EC22.

claims.proposition: Cryptocurrency's status as property does not itself establish customer beneficial ownership.

support.quote: Cryptocurrency is “property” and is capable of being held on trust
However, the terms of the 2018 T&C show that there was no certainty of intention to create a trust over the cryptocurrencies held by Gatecoin
Except the Non-Consenting Customers, the fiat currencies are not held by Gatecoin on trust for the Customers

claims.inference: Text: the 2023 conclusion distinguishes the capacity of cryptocurrency to be trust property from whether this particular relationship created a trust.
missing_premises: The applicable customer terms and evidence establishing whether the customer falls within the non-consenting exception.
Full reasons needed to determine the precise ratio and its reach beyond the retained passages.

claims.proposition: Ownership labels and agency relationships are relevant but not conclusive evidence of a trust.

support.quote: The words used by the parties such as ‘trust’, ‘custody’, ‘belonging’, ‘ownership’, ‘title’, may be persuasive, but they are not conclusive in favour of the recognition of B’s proprietary interest in the property, if the terms of the agreement or relationship, viewed objectively, compel a different conclusion.

The identification of a relationship in which A is B’s agent or broker is not conclusive of a conclusion that A is, in relation to the property, B’s trustee, although it may be a pointer towards that conclusion.

claims.inference: Text: the judgment quotes principles attributed to Briggs J in Re Lehman Brothers. Deduction: descriptions of custody or ownership cannot substitute for assessment of the actual agreement and relationship.
missing_premises: The complete contractual and factual relationship for each pair of parties.
The governing law and requirements for recognising the asserted proprietary interest.

claims.proposition: Customer consent requires transaction-specific evidence rather than inference from a ledger timestamp alone.

support.quote: The customers should be regarded as NCCs unless there is evidence to show that they have accessed or used the Platform to effect the transactions

The transactions described in the 5th to 6th scenarios on their face required the customers to access or use the Platform to effect them and, prima facie, the customers fall outside the definition of NCC.
However, if the customers are able to prove that they gave the instruction to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

claims.inference: Text: paragraph 8 uses rebuttable, evidence-dependent classifications. Deduction: transactions recorded after the relevant date do not uniformly establish acceptance through platform use.
missing_premises: Customer-specific platform-access records, instruction dates and means of instruction.
The complete definition of NCC and applicable evidential requirements.

claims.proposition: The 2025 conclusions differ by party, property and legal relationship.

support.quote: Each NCC is a beneficial tenant-in-common in a pool of cryptocurrency and fiat currency.
The Currencies recorded in BlueFire’s accounts are assets of Gatecoin.
ETD represents a cause of action by ETD Holder against Gatecoin for breach of trust.
Gatecoin does not hold the Subject Bitcoins or the Specified Account on trust for Mr Samara.
Mr Samara is only an unsecured creditor to the extent of his claim less the amount he already received through execution of the HCA Judgment.

claims.inference: Text: the 2025 passages distinguish beneficial ownership in pools, ownership of assets recorded in another party's accounts, breach-of-trust claims and unsecured claims. Deduction: these relationships cannot be collapsed into a general token-holder ownership rule.
missing_premises: The full reasons and facts supporting each distinct relationship.
Pool composition, shortfalls, administration costs and proof of each claimant's entitlement for any distribution calculation.

claims.proposition: The retained text does not support an unqualified executable classifier for scenario seven.

support.quote: The transactions described in the 7th scenario did not exist and the customers should not be regarded as NCC.

The 5th to 7th scenarios prima facie fall outside the definition of NCC but if the customers can prove that they gave the relevant instructions to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

Any Customer who claims to have transactions enumerated in paragraphs 1.2(b) shall notify the Liquidators and provide evidence to the Liquidators in support of such a claim within 21 days from the date hereof.

claims.inference: Text comparison: paragraph 8 rejects the factual existence of scenario seven, whereas paragraph 95 includes it in a group admitting an evidential exception. The annexure states particular classifications and a deadline; it does not expressly resolve that discrepancy.
missing_premises: A justified reconciliation of paragraphs 8 and 95 with the annexure, based on full reasons and operative directions.
Any relevant correction or subsequent judicial clarification.

claims.proposition: Gatecoin trust conclusions do not establish either the applicability or fulfillment of a Product Provider's regulatory requirements.

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

claims.inference: Proposed legal comparison: Gatecoin may inform analysis of proprietary interests, but the retained judgments do not interpret 26EC22. Paragraphs 10 and 11 separately address continuing responsibility and proper ownership records. Transfer requires a reasoned analogy, not merely a shared use of cryptocurrency.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained 26EC22 edition to the entity, product, activity and assessment period, including conditions and amendments.
Proof of Product Provider status and identification of any separate trustee, custodian, register keeper or intermediary capacities.
Identification of the token, underlying product interest and property allegedly held on trust, with governing terms, consent evidence and applicable law.
A checked proposition from the full judgments, its authority and subsequent treatment, and reasons material factual differences do not defeat the analogy.
An applicable fulfillment standard and actual evidence of management, operational soundness and proper ownership records.

claims.proposition: The retained 2025 passage records the 2023 conclusions; broader authority status remains unresolved.

support.quote: In summary, it was held that: Cryptocurrency is property and is capable of being held on trust; With the exception of the Non-consenting Customers (“NCCs”), the 2018 T&C applied to, and governed the relationship between all the Customers (be it Group A, B or C) and Gatecoin.

claims.inference: Text: the 2025 judgment expressly recounts the earlier conclusions. Judgment on evidentiary limits: this supports continuity within these proceedings, but does not establish complete subsequent treatment or binding force for a different dispute.
missing_premises: Complete subsequent treatment through the relevant assessment date.
The applicable precedential framework and full reasons establishing the proposed ratio.

rival_readings: Scenario seven: paragraph 8 supports exclusion because the transactions did not exist; paragraph 95's literal wording includes scenario seven within a potentially rebuttable exclusion. Neither reading is conclusively preferred here.

The annexure may particularise the operative classifications, but treating it as resolving every discrepancy with paragraphs 8 and 95 requires an interpretive warrant absent from the retained passages.
Gatecoin can inform an analogy about objectively assessed ownership relationships; treating it as a direct construction or fulfillment test for 26EC22 is unsupported.
unresolved: Full reasons, precise ratio, complete subsequent treatment and target-specific precedential force have not been established.
Scenario-seven wording and the annexure require reconciliation before complete customer classification is claimed.
No actual Product Provider terms, consent records, operational evidence or applicable fulfillment standard are supplied.

Source identity checks, graph acceptance and rule round-tripping do not establish legal truth. The shared case-manifest hash identifies the combined packet; the individual DOCX hashes identify different source objects.
The retained case passages are selected extracts with no rendered-document fidelity certification.
